passage:
A family found a damaged photo of their great-grandparents. The faces were scratched, and one corner was missing.
A photo shop used digital tools to restore it. The new version looked clear, but the family kept the damaged original too.
The youngest child asked why they needed both. Her mother said the restored photo helped them see the people better. The damaged photo showed time itself.
Both versions told the truth in different ways.
Digital repair can bring the past closer, but marks and scratches also carry history. Not every imperfection should be erased completely. Sometimes damage is part of the object's journey.
